thread.title: UPDATE: Facebook earnings send stock toward record after massive ad price increase

author: morningstar.com
title: UPDATE: Facebook earnings send stock toward record after massive ad price increase
text:
By Max A. Cherney
Average price for Facebook ads jumped 43% in fourth quarter
Facebook Inc. shares reversed course to show gains in late trading Wednesday after the company reported double-digit advertising price growth amid massive changes to its core product.
After dropping as much as 5% after fourth-quarter earnings revealed a tax charge and reduced time spent by users on the platform, Facebook shares (FB) swung as high as $194.50 during the earnings call as executives discussed ad pricing growth. Facebook stock has never traded higher than $190.66 in regular trading, and shares dipped back below that level later in the after-hours session.
The stock losses swung to gains after Chief Financial Officer David Wehner, in prepared remarks on a post-earnings conference call, said that the average price per Facebook ad increased by 43% as the total number of impressions -- pages loaded with ads served by Facebook -- gained 4% last quarter. The majority of the pricing increase is due to Facebook's core app as well as Instagram, for which it does not break out financial results (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-youtube-and-instagram-secret-that-google-and-facebook-dont-want-you-to-know-2018-01-26).
More:Facebook stock heads for record after earnings show ad prices increasing: live blog recap (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/facebook-earnings-to-provide-insight-into-news-feed-changes-live-blog-2018-01-31)
"So you can think of all these ... optimization efforts as part of that as being an effort to improve the yield of the impressions that we have to drive downstream business results for our advertising partners," Wehner said on the call. "And if we can drive those effectively, that will translate into higher effective prices for our business."
Heading in to the earnings call, it was an open question as to how much the massive changes to the company's news feed and other products (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/how-facebooks-newsfeed-change-is-stoking-uncertainty-about-its-future-2018-01-13) would affect the company's top and bottom line. Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg addressed the apparent effects thus far of early changes targeting viral videos, and said that users spent about 50 million fewer hours a day on the platform, or just more than two minutes a day per worldwide daily user.
In a note to clients late Wednesday, Baird analyst Colin Sebastian wrote that the changes suggest that the "platform remains quite healthy" despite ongoing concerns about "user engagement and potential adverse effects of social media remain elevated."
Sebastian rates Facebook the equivalent of a buy with a $200 price target.
The changes to the Facebook platform did lead to the reduction of about 700,000 daily active users in the U.S. and Canada, regions where each user was worth $26.76 in the fourth quarter, compared with the worldwide average of $6.18. Europe is the next most valuable region, with users worth about $8.86 apiece per quarter.
Read:The YouTube and Instagram secret that Google and Facebook don't want you to know (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-youtube-and-instagram-secret-that-google-and-facebook-dont-want-you-to-know-2018-01-26)
Compared with the year-ago quarter, the rates of impressions growth and ad price growth have flipped: In 2016's fourth quarter, impressions grew by 49% and ad prices went up by 3%. But since the beginning of 2017, Facebook's ad impression growth has decelerated incrementally from 32% in the first quarter, sending prices up.
The refrain is a familiar one to Facebook watchers -- as the amount of ad inventory grows more slowly and advertisers still hunger to spend dollars there, the price goes up. To wit, in 2015's first quarter, Facebook served 62% fewer impressions, sending ad prices up a whopping 285%.
One little talked about and little noticed element of Facebook financial statements is the company's payments category. For the first time in three years, payments revenue grew from the previous year, ticking up 7% to $193 million. It's not entirely clear why that was the case, though the growth was entirely in the Asia-Pacific region.
Marketplace could be one of the reasons, if users are transacting more across Facebook's version of eBay. Executives on the call said that "more than 700 million people each month now come to Facebook to buy and sell things" and that it launched the product in 41 countries throughout 2017.
While repeating one of Facebook executives' favored refrains on earnings calls -- "it's early days" -- Chief Operating Officer Sheryl Sandberg also called commerce an "important vertical" in the company's ad business and "that commerce discovering products all the way through the sale is a big part of what's driving our ads business."
Like many U.S. companies, Facebook also logged a charge of $2.27 billion, or 77 cents a share related to changes in the U.S. tax code in the fourth quarter.
For more: Tax bill lowered corporate tax rate, so why are some companies announcing charges? (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/tax-bill-lowered-corporate-tax-rate-so-why-are-some-companies-announcing-charges-2018-01-18)
Facebook is one of six companies that have topped a $500 billion (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/techs-500-billion-club-has-tripled-and-it-dominates-the-market-as-earnings-storm-approaches-2018-01-30) market valuation and are reporting results Wednesday and Thursday (the others are Alibaba Group Holding Ltd.(BABA), Google parent Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL) (GOOGL) , Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) and Apple Inc. (AAPL)) . Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) , one of the six, also reported earnings Wednesday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/shares-of-microsoft-slide-as-software-giant-reports-a-quarterly-loss-on-tax-cuts-2018-01-31).
Facebook stock has gained 43% in the past 12 months, with the S&P 500 index gaining 24% in that time.
-Max A. Cherney;
